title: Auto tone for the Basic panel
objective: Deliver a deterministic, explainable Auto tone that sets Lightroom's eight Basic fields (Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Vibrance, Saturation) on the global Basic layer as one undoable entry, from a bounded analysis sample of the stage Basic receives, with a command and query for API parity, a desktop Auto button, Auto in presets and the Lightroom importer, then fit its targets to Lightroom's Auto on the owner's photos.
context_summary: The owner requested a plan and decided scope on 2026-10-07: Lightroom's eight sliders, no white balance, Auto in presets (recomputed per photo) and AutoTone import mapping, and tuning by fitting to Lightroom's Auto on the owner's photos after delivery. Implementation is not authorized by the planning request. Deterministic statistics and searches (no learned model), analysis before Basic with a forward model through Basic and the Look only, the starting targets, grid size, caps, button placement and Cmd+U are recorded defaults in the design; routine organisation is delegated. The solver and the analysis sample are independent outputs consumed by the action; desktop and presets build on the action; the Lightroom rig needs only the solver; the owner's export is the one external input and is needed only by the final fit. Re-review against current main and use the roadmap high-tier model minimum. No approval, owner-question or research task is inserted.

tasks.description: Implement the auto-tone/1 solver as a pure core function over an analysis sample, with versioned targets and an explanation report.
extra_context: Deliver the solver, AutoToneTargets (auto-tone/1 constants from the design) and the bounded explanation consumed by TASK-003 and TASK-007. No sample reading, command, UI or preset change here.

Input: a sample of linear RGB f32 values with per-sample exclusion flags (non-finite, source white), plus the compiled pointwise units of a candidate global Basic payload followed by the global Look layer when present. Reuse the modules' own compiled units; add no second copy of Basic or Look equations.

Steps in fixed order: Exposure median target with the bright-fraction guard; Highlights and Shadows from band fractions; Contrast from the P90-P10 spread; Whites and Blacks binary searches on their integer grids to the 0.05% clipping fractions with source-white samples excluded; one second sweep of Exposure, Whites and Blacks; Vibrance and Saturation from mean Oklab chroma. Round to field steps half away from zero; every search runs on the committed grid.

Statistics in f64 with deterministic weighted reductions so results are independent of thread count. Repeated evaluation may use a reduced sample only where tests prove equal fractions and percentiles to brute force over the whole sample.
Refuse fewer than 1,024 usable samples, an input luminance spread P99-P1 under half a stop, or a median at or below 1e-6, with a structured reason.
The implementer chooses module placement within luxforge-core and the reduction strategy.

acceptance_criteria: Hand-computed synthetic samples (dark, bright, low contrast, high key, clipped source, saturated colour, near-neutral) produce the expected values; degenerate samples are refused with their reasons.
Each committed Whites/Blacks value meets its clipping constraint and the next step outward fails it; Exposure meets the median and bright-guard rules on its 0.01 EV grid.
Results are identical across Rayon thread counts and repeated runs; solving with Basic already at the result gives the same values.
Every value stays within its declared Auto bound and the field's range; bounded fields are listed in the explanation, which stays within 4 KiB and names the forward-model layers.
A Look present in the forward model changes the result consistently with rendering the same payload through the reference renderer on the sample's values.

steps: Write independent oracle tests with hand-computed statistics and brute-force evaluation over small samples; do not mirror the solver's code.
Exercise thread-count determinism, idempotence, bounds and refusals.
expected_results: All solver tests pass; no frame rendering, IO or owner-thread work is introduced.

tasks.description: Provide a bounded, identity-keyed analysis sample of the stage the Basic layer receives through the deferred tile-service read path, on the GPU and the reference.
extra_context: Deliver the sample read consumed by TASK-003: a grid of at most 1024 points on the output frame's long side at pixel centres, each mapped back through the stack's geometry (crop, straighten, lens, perspective) to the Basic input stage and read as that stage's linear values at the nearest input pixel, without interpolation. Points outside the input stage are dropped.

Extend the existing deferred read path (TileSession::read with ReadStage::Before) from a patch to a bounded strided grid. The GPU gathers from prefix tiles with no full-frame CPU buffer; the reference may borrow an already-held frame and otherwise renders through its tiles. Never read on the catalog owner.
Flag non-finite samples and samples at the source's white in any channel (JPEG code 255; RAW sensor saturation where the development reports it).

Identity: asset, source fingerprint, content of layers before Basic, geometry after Basic, grid dimensions, renderer and algorithm; it excludes Basic's own values and later colour layers. Retain samples within a 32 MiB total cap, released on photo replacement and leaving Develop; charge scratch before allocation; cancel at chunk granularity.
The implementer chooses the read plumbing and storage format within these caps.

acceptance_criteria: The reference sample equals an independent grid read of the reference frame exactly, including crop, straighten, lens and perspective geometry, JPEG and RAW kinds.
The GPU sample matches the reference sample within the declared display tolerance on generated and supplied RAW inputs.

A repeated read with equal identity reuses the retained sample with no render; changing Basic, the Look or a later colour layer does not invalidate it, while a layer before Basic or geometry after it does.
Storage stays within the caps including replacement; cancellation and photo switches never deliver a stale sample; no read runs on the owner thread and the original is never re-read.

Compare GPU and reference samples on the M4 within tolerance; test cancellation, identity reuse and caps.
expected_results: Exact reference and in-tolerance GPU samples, reuse by identity and bounded storage are demonstrated.

tasks.description: Add Basic's auto-tone action and query, committing one Auto tone entry on the global Basic layer with API parity.
extra_context: edit.auto-tone {asset_id, mutation} analyses the current revision and creates or updates the one global Basic layer, writing all eight fields absolutely and leaving Temperature, Tint and set-raw untouched; equal result is a no-op. query.auto-tone {asset_id, entry_id?} returns values and the explanation without committing. Both share one function.
The action takes no parameters, is not a field patch or draft action, and plans through the deferred read path; the owner handles metadata only.

Label the entry Auto tone; it does not collapse into following slider edits. Refuse a mask target (validation: Auto tone applies to the photo's global Basic layer), a historical selection and an open draft as Basic actions are refused; surface solver refusals with their reason.
Register both in the module descriptor so schema.list discovers them with notes describing behaviour.

tasks.description: Carry Auto tone in presets as a per-photo analysis step, with capture, the create form and Lightroom AutoTone import mapping.
extra_context: A settings set may name "auto-tone": {} (the one key allowed an empty object); a registry answer beside patch_action declares analysis-step actions. The step runs after every field-patch step whatever the key order and analyses the intermediate stack through the same deferred read; other composites keep planning without rasterizing.
Refuse at store a set naming auto-tone together with any of its eight set-basic fields. A degenerate photo skips the step and reports it under skipped; the rest of the preset applies.
preset.capture accepts {"auto-tone": true}; the desktop create form gains an Auto tone row in Basic's Tone group that clears and disables the eight fields.

Import: crs:AutoTone True (XMP) and AutoTone = true (.lrtemplate) map to the step; the eight fields in that preset are reported as overridden by Auto tone; False is neutral; earlier process versions' Auto* switches keep their current treatment. The Luxforge preset document round-trips the key.
batch.apply-preset continues to apply through edit.apply-preset per photo, so each photo is analysed separately.

tasks.description: Build the Lightroom Auto fitting rig: picture statistics, target fitting with hold-out, and a report, proven on synthetic and corpus inputs before the owner's export exists.
extra_context: Rust tooling only. Inputs: originals, Lightroom's Auto-result sRGB JPEG exports and XMP sidecars. Compute the picture statistics the solver uses (median, P10/P90, band fractions, clipping fractions, mean chroma) on Lightroom's exports and on Luxforge's Auto output for the same originals, and fit AutoToneTargets to minimise a weighted median difference with a quarter held out.

Compare in picture space so the fit does not depend on the unfinished slider response alignment; report base-rendering differences beside it, and compare slider values for information using alignment conversions where they exist.
Rendered outputs only, no Adobe code or data; runs locally, keeps figures only, asks consent each run when given the owner's photos.
Prove the rig end to end with synthetic stand-ins for Lightroom's exports (for example Luxforge's own Auto at perturbed targets, which the fit must recover).
